concepts.def: There are three types of strong chemical bond: ionic, covalent and metallic. All three are electrostatic in origin, but they differ in which particles are held together and in what happens to the outer electrons.
Bonding in which the particles are oppositely charged ions. It occurs in compounds formed from metals combined with non-metals.
Bonding in which the particles are atoms which share pairs of electrons. It occurs in most non-metallic elements and in compounds of non-metals.
Bonding in which the particles are atoms which share delocalised electrons. It occurs in metallic elements and in alloys.

The force of attraction between opposite electric charges. Chemical bonding is explained by electrostatic attraction: between positive and negative ions, between two nuclei and a shared pair of electrons, or between metal ions and the sea of delocalised electrons.
The movement of electrons from the outer shell of a metal atom to the outer shell of a non-metal atom when the two react. Transfer produces ions; it is not itself the bond.
An ion formed when a metal atom loses one or more electrons from its outer shell. It has more protons than electrons, so its charge is positive.
An ion formed when a non-metal atom gains one or more electrons into its outer shell. It has more electrons than protons, so its charge is negative.
The full outer shell arrangement of a Group 0 element. The ions produced by metals in Groups 1 and 2 and by non-metals in Groups 6 and 7 have the electronic structure of a noble gas.
A diagram that shows the electron transfer forming an ionic compound, using dots for the electrons of one atom and crosses for the other, so that the origin of each electron can be followed.
For the elements in scope, the charge on the ion follows from the group number: Group 1 forms 1+, Group 2 forms 2+, Group 6 forms 2- and Group 7 forms 1-.
An ionic compound is a giant structure of ions, held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions. There are no separate molecules in it.
In an ionic lattice the electrostatic forces act in all directions, not along a fixed line between two chosen ions. This is what is meant by ionic bonding.
The structure of sodium chloride can be shown as a two-dimensional diagram, as a three-dimensional ball and stick model or as a space-filling model. Each is a model of the same giant lattice.

concepts.term: Empirical formula of an ionic compound
concepts.def: The simplest whole number ratio of the ions in the structure. It is worked out from a model or diagram by counting the ions of each type and cancelling to the simplest ratio.

A ball and stick model shows gaps between ions that do not exist and sticks that are not real; a two-dimensional diagram shows forces in only two directions; no diagram can show the full extent of the lattice.

When atoms share pairs of electrons they form covalent bonds, and these bonds between atoms are strong. The strength of the bonds inside a molecule says nothing about the melting or boiling point of the substance.
A covalently bonded substance may consist of small molecules, each containing a small fixed number of non-metal atoms, such as H2, Cl2, HCl, H2O, NH3, CH4 and CO2.
A covalently bonded substance whose molecules are very large: many small molecules joined into long chains. A polymer has very large molecules, not a giant structure.
A structure in which very many atoms are joined by covalent bonds throughout the whole structure, with no separate molecules. Diamond and silicon dioxide are the specification's examples.

concepts.term: Dot and cross diagram of a molecule
concepts.def: A diagram showing the shared pairs of electrons in a molecule, using dots and crosses to show which atom each electron came from. Required for hydrogen, chlorine, oxygen, nitrogen, hydrogen chloride, water, ammonia and methane.
A polymer is represented by its repeating unit drawn in brackets with a subscript n, where n is a large number. It is not a value to be calculated from the diagram.
In a displayed formula or a diagram of a giant structure, one line between two atoms represents one single covalent bond, that is one shared pair of electrons.
A dot and cross diagram shows the electrons but not the shape or size; a two-dimensional diagram flattens a three-dimensional molecule; a ball and stick model exaggerates the space between atoms.
The molecular formula is deduced by counting the atoms of each element shown in the model or diagram. The bonds, sticks or lines are not counted, and the number is not reduced to the simplest ratio.
Metals consist of giant structures of atoms arranged in a regular pattern.

An electron from the outer shell of a metal atom that is no longer held by one atom and is free to move through the whole structure. Sharing these delocalised electrons gives rise to strong metallic bonds.
A mixture containing a metal and one or more other elements. The bonding in an alloy is metallic, as it is in a pure metallic element.

mcqs.q: The specification describes covalent bonding in terms of which particles?
options: ions which have swapped electron pairs
atoms sharing delocalised electrons
atoms which share pairs of electrons
electrons moving from atom to atom
mcqs.explain: This is the specification's wording: for covalent bonding the particles are atoms which share pairs of electrons.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a compound held together by ionic bonding?
options: lithium fluoride, a metal and a non-metal
sulfur dioxide, a compound of two elements
hydrogen chloride, a gas containing chloride
nitrogen gas, an element with very strong bonds
mcqs.explain: Lithium is a metal and fluorine a non-metal, which is exactly the condition the specification gives for ionic bonding.

mcqs.q: Covalent bonding occurs in which of these?
options: compounds of non-metals only, never in elements
any compound made from two different elements
non-metals combined with metals in a lattice
most non-metallic elements and non-metal compounds
mcqs.explain: This is the specification statement: covalent bonding occurs in most non-metallic elements and in compounds of non-metals.

mcqs.q: Brass is an alloy of copper and zinc. Which type of bonding does it have?
options: ionic, because it contains two different elements
metallic, because alloys bond like pure metals
ionic, since positive ions attract negative ions
covalent, as the atoms share outer electrons
mcqs.explain: The specification states that metallic bonding occurs in metallic elements and alloys.

mcqs.q: In terms of electrostatic forces, what is the ionic bond in sodium chloride?
options: attraction between oppositely charged ions
the movement of an electron across the bond
a pair of electrons shared by the ions
attraction between the two atomic nuclei
mcqs.explain: Chemical bonding is explained by electrostatic forces; in an ionic compound these act between the positive and negative ions.

mcqs.q: Which statement correctly links the three bond types to what happens to the outer electrons?
options: ionic and metallic share electrons; covalent transfers
all three types involve sharing pairs of electrons
ionic transfers electrons; covalent and metallic share them
covalent shares electrons; ionic and metallic do not
mcqs.explain: Ionic bonding transfers electrons, covalent bonding shares pairs between atoms and metallic bonding shares delocalised electrons.

mcqs.q: A magnesium atom reacts with oxygen. What happens to magnesium's outer electrons?
options: six more are gained for a full outer shell
they are lost, giving a 2- charged ion
they are shared with the oxygen atom
they are transferred, giving a 2+ ion
mcqs.explain: Metal atoms lose the electrons in their outer shell and become positively charged ions.

mcqs.q: Which ions have the electronic structure of a noble gas?
options: none, since an ion keeps its structure
those formed by Groups 1, 2, 6 and 7
only those whose charge equals the group
only metal ions, since they lose electrons
mcqs.explain: The specification names exactly these: ions produced by metals in Groups 1 and 2 and by non-metals in Groups 6 and 7.

mcqs.q: A sodium atom, 2,8,1, forms a sodium ion. What is the ion's electronic structure and charge?
options: 2,8 with a charge of 1+, the same as neon
2,8,8 with a charge of 7-, like argon
2,8,1 with a 1+ charge, shells unchanged
2,8 but with a 1- charge, like neon
mcqs.explain: One outer electron is lost, leaving a full second shell and one more proton than electron.

mcqs.q: In a dot and cross diagram of sodium chloride, how is the sodium ion drawn?
options: in brackets with a 1+ charge and one outer electron
with an arrow showing the electron crossing over
in brackets with a 1+ charge, outer shell empty
with one outer electron and no charge shown
mcqs.explain: The transferred electron is drawn in the chlorine outer shell, so it is not drawn on sodium as well.

mcqs.q: Which dot and cross diagram represents magnesium chloride?
options: one Mg2+ ion drawn with a single Cl- ion
one Mg2+ ion drawn with two Cl- ions
two Mg2+ ions drawn with a Cl2- ion
one Mg2- ion next to two Cl+ ions
mcqs.explain: Magnesium loses two electrons, one to each chlorine atom, so the ratio is one to two.

mcqs.q: Which pairing of group and ionic charge is correct?
options: Group 6 forms an ion carrying a 6- charge
Group 2 forms an ion with a charge of 2-
Group 7 forms a 7+ ion, from its group number
Group 6 forms an ion with a 2- charge
mcqs.explain: A Group 6 atom gains two electrons to reach a full outer shell, so the charge is 2-.

mcqs.q: Calcium is in Group 2 and fluorine in Group 7. Which pair of ions do they form?
options: Ca2+ and F-, since calcium loses two
Ca2+ and F7-, taken from the group numbers
Ca2- and F+, as calcium gains electrons
Ca2+ and F2-, so the formula is CaF
mcqs.explain: Group 2 metals lose two electrons to form 2+ ions; Group 7 non-metals gain one to form 1- ions.

mcqs.q: Potassium is in Group 1 and oxygen in Group 6. What is the formula of the compound formed?
options: KO, because one ion of each is enough
K2O, as two 1+ ions balance one 2- ion
K6O, read from the two group numbers
KO2, since oxygen forms two bonds
mcqs.explain: Potassium forms K+ and oxygen forms O2-, so two potassium ions are needed for each oxide ion.

mcqs.q: What holds an ionic compound together?
options: strong bonds pointing from each ion to its partner
pairs of electrons shared between the ions
attraction between ions and loose electrons
strong electrostatic forces between charged ions
mcqs.explain: The specification states that ionic compounds are held together by strong electrostatic forces of attraction between oppositely charged ions.

mcqs.q: Why does the specification say that the forces in an ionic lattice act in all directions?
options: each ion is bonded to one partner ion only
the bonds point along fixed lines like sticks
each ion attracts oppositely charged ions around it
the ions only touch where the sticks join them
mcqs.explain: The attraction is between oppositely charged ions and is not confined to a line, so it holds the whole lattice together.

mcqs.q: A diagram shows a regular cube of alternating small and large spheres, one element a metal. What is it?
options: separate molecules of the compound stacked up
a metal, as its atoms form a regular pattern
a giant covalent structure of shared pairs
a giant ionic lattice with the ions alternating
mcqs.explain: A regular alternating array of two elements, one a metal, is the giant ionic structure of a compound such as sodium chloride.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a limitation of a ball and stick model of sodium chloride?
options: the sticks suggest gaps between the ions
it shows the compound as separate molecules
it shows forces in two directions only
it cannot show a regular arrangement
mcqs.explain: In the real lattice the ions touch; the gaps and sticks exist only to make the arrangement visible.

mcqs.q: A model of an ionic compound shows 8 magnesium ions and 16 chloride ions. What is the empirical formula?
options: Mg8Cl16, the numbers counted in the model
MgCl, since the ions pair up one to one
MgCl2, the simplest whole number ratio
Mg2Cl, with the larger number first
mcqs.explain: Eight to sixteen reduces to one to two, and an empirical formula is always the simplest ratio.

mcqs.q: Water boils at 100 C. What does this tell you about the covalent bonds within a water molecule?
options: they are weak, since water boils easily
nothing; the bonds in it are strong
they break when the water turns to steam
they are weaker than ionic bonds are
mcqs.explain: Boiling separates whole molecules from each other. The bonds between atoms inside the molecule are strong and unaffected.

mcqs.q: Which of these substances consists of small molecules?
options: NaCl, a short two-symbol formula
SiO2, which looks just like CO2
CH4, a compound of two non-metals
MgO, a compound made of two elements
mcqs.explain: Carbon and hydrogen are both non-metals, and methane is one of the small molecules named in the specification.

mcqs.q: Poly(ethene) is a covalently bonded substance with very large molecules. What does that mean?
options: its molecules are very large but separate
it has a giant covalent structure like diamond
the covalent bonds in it must be weaker
it is a mixture of very many small molecules
mcqs.explain: A polymer consists of very large molecules; each chain is a separate molecule.

mcqs.q: Which pair of substances both have giant covalent structures?
options: carbon dioxide and silicon dioxide, two oxides
diamond and silicon dioxide, the named examples
poly(ethene) and diamond, both very large
sodium chloride and diamond, both giant
mcqs.explain: These are the two giant covalent structures given in the specification.

mcqs.q: In the representation of a polymer, what does n stand for?
options: a number you work out from the diagram
the count of carbon atoms in the unit
the simplest whole number ratio of atoms
a large number of repeating units
mcqs.explain: The specification states only that n is a large number.

mcqs.q: How many shared pairs of electrons are there between the atoms in an oxygen molecule, O2?
options: two, drawn as four electrons in the overlap
one, since a covalent bond is one shared pair
four, one for each electron in the overlap
six, since each atom has six outer electrons
mcqs.explain: Each oxygen atom needs two more electrons, so two pairs are shared: a double bond.

mcqs.q: In the displayed formula of methane, what does each of the four lines represent?
options: one electron passed from carbon to hydrogen
the two electrons carbon contributes
a stick that holds the two atoms apart
one single bond, that is one shared pair
mcqs.explain: A line is used to represent a single covalent bond, which is one shared pair of electrons.

mcqs.q: What is a limitation of a two-dimensional displayed formula of a methane molecule?
options: it shows the atoms at their true relative size
it gives the ratio of atoms, not the number
it does not show the real shape of the molecule
it shows each bond as a single electron
mcqs.explain: A flat drawing cannot show that the four bonds point to the corners of a tetrahedron.

mcqs.q: A model of ethene shows two black balls (carbon), four white balls (hydrogen) and six sticks. What is the molecular formula?
options: CH2, the simplest whole number ratio
C2H4, counting only the balls
C2H6, one hydrogen for each stick
C6H4, taking the sticks as carbons
mcqs.explain: The molecular formula counts the atoms shown: two carbon and four hydrogen.

mcqs.q: How are the atoms arranged in a pure metal?
options: in a giant structure with a regular pattern
randomly, in a closely packed jumble of atoms
a lattice of positive and negative ions
in small groups of a few joined atoms
mcqs.explain: The specification states that metals consist of giant structures of atoms arranged in a regular pattern.

mcqs.q: Which statement about the electrons in a metal is correct?
options: each atom keeps its outer electrons, loosely
every electron in every atom is delocalised
the outer electrons are free to move about
the electrons are transferred to the ions
mcqs.explain: The electrons in the outer shell of metal atoms are delocalised and so are free to move through the whole structure.

mcqs.q: In terms of electrostatic forces, what is a covalent bond?
options: attraction between the shared pair and both nuclei
attraction between the two positive nuclei
attraction between ions and delocalised electrons
an electron moving from one atom to the other
mcqs.explain: The shared pair of electrons is attracted to the nuclei of both bonded atoms, and that attraction is the bond.

mcqs.q: What gives rise to the strong metallic bonds in copper?
options: attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons
attraction between positive and negative ions
shared pairs of electrons between two metal atoms
each atom holding on to its own outer electrons
mcqs.explain: The sharing of delocalised electrons gives strong metallic bonds: the positive metal ions are attracted to the electrons.
